title: Waitlist and capacity for autism-focused Day Activity Centres
asked: Ms Kuah Boon Theng asked how many people with autism spectrum disorder are currently waitlisted for a Day Activity Centre place, what the average wait is, and whether more places will be made available for them.
response: Mr Eric Chua said eight DACs specialise in serving clients with ASD, with 130 people on the waitlist and an average waiting time of nine months for enrolment. MSF is adding 500 DAC places, as announced in its 2024 Committee of Supply, and he said the Ministry is prepared to work with private providers and is looking at different service models. He pointed to pilots such as the Enabled Living Programme, the Home Support Programme starting in the second half of this year, three Enabling Services Hubs, and the Enabling Skills for Life Programme, and said an inter-agency task force headed by Minister of State Goh Pei Ming is looking at affordability of services. In a later reply he said DAC spaces will increase by 500 over the next few years by 2030, with more if there is an assessed need.

left_open: Whether the average wait time differs by type of DAC, including the suggestion that waits at some larger centres can reach five years or more.
Whether waitlist numbers reflect actual demand, given families who leave the waitlist and the cost of DAC fees for families earning above $2,800 a month.
Whether subsidies could be extended to help more families afford DAC fees.
How capacity and resources will be directed specifically at those with high support needs.
